ref-0001.customer: Parent (NZ/AU) of children roughly 3-10 with a backyard, comparing play forts/climbing frames against swing sets and treehouse kits; budget- and safety-conscious, browsing on a phone in the evening. Five questions: (1) How much is it? (2) Will it fit in my backyard? (3) Is it safe - will it tip over, how high is the drop? (4) What ages is it for - will they outgrow it? (5) Can I actually buy it now, and how hard is it to put up?

five_questions_test.question: How much does it cost?
five_questions_test.where: nowhere - no price on any desktop or mobile screenshot; only 'Get updates' and an email list (mobile-page-07, desktop-page-08)

five_questions_test.question: Will it fit in my backyard?
five_questions_test.where: mobile-page-06 / desktop-page-06-07: dimension drawing (3140 mm tall, 1200/1700 mm footprint) with child silhouette and 'Small enough for real gardens'; night photo beside a house in mobile-page-04 / desktop-page-04

five_questions_test.question: Is it safe - will it tip over?
five_questions_test.where: desktop-page-04 'Dangerously safe ... resist toppling ... ground anchors ... designed to ISO 8124:4, NZ certification pending'; on mobile it is carousel card 2, cut off at the right edge of mobile-page-03 and never shown

five_questions_test.question: What ages is it for / will they outgrow it?
five_questions_test.where: not stated anywhere; only inferable from photos of ~5-10 year olds (mobile-page-02/03/08) and the child silhouette (mobile-page-06)

five_questions_test.question: Can I buy it now, and how hard is it to put up?
five_questions_test.where: mobile-page-07 / desktop-page-07-08: 'Delivered flat-packed ... assembled by two adults in a morning'; 'released in limited production runs. Join the list' - i.e. you cannot buy it; accessories 'Coming soon' (mobile-page-05)

reasons.customer:
Answers fit, assembly and (on desktop) toppling in concrete parent-friendly terms, but price and age range are absent and the only action is joining an email list.
On mobile the fold has no words about what the product is, safety copy sits in an off-screen carousel card, and a transparent sticky logo collides with body text on most screens.

claims.evidence: Partly earned: the night shot of the fort next to a weatherboard house (mobile-page-04, desktop-page-04) and kids climbing/pointing (mobile-page-02/03, desktop-page-03) answer 'what does it look like in a real garden' and roughly 'what age kids use it'. Limits: the mobile and desktop folds are a 3D render with colour swatches, not a photo; photos carry no captions, so they answer no question about price, age or safety; the most useful visual for 'will it fit' is the dimension drawing (mobile-page-06), which is a diagram, not photography. Photography sets the mood more than it answers questions.

take: Scale drawing + human silhouette + one plain sentence: show exact dimensions (mm) next to a child figure and say the outcome in the buyer's words ('Small enough for real gardens') - mobile-page-06.
Effort in human units: state installation as people x time ('assembled by two adults in a morning') instead of specs - mobile-page-07.
Context photo in a real setting: show the product beside a normal house at dusk so a parent can picture it in their own yard - mobile-page-04.
avoid: No price, no age range and no way to buy: the page's only conversion is 'Get updates'/email list (mobile-page-07), so a comparing parent leaves with nothing to compare.

Unreadable or colliding text: colour labels measured 1.14:1 ('Sand') and 1.16:1 ('Yellow'), hero intro white on #edbf7a = 1.70:1; the transparent sticky 'Playfolly' logo overlaps body copy on mobile-page-02/05/06/07 and desktop-page-04/06/07/08.

Key answer hidden behind interaction: the safety copy is in carousel card 2, off-screen on mobile (mobile-page-03); carousel buttons measured 12x48 px (7 controls under 24 px); without JavaScript 0 of 3144 characters are visible.
missed_by_note: Price is absent everywhere - the first question every comparing parent asks.
No age range or weight limit is stated.

The mobile fold (mobile-fold.png) has zero explanatory words - a vertical wordmark, a render and colour swatches - so a first-time phone visitor does not learn what the product is until the next screen.
Safety answer is effectively invisible on mobile (off-screen carousel card).
Sticky transparent logo overlaps running text on most mobile and desktop screens.
Report flags the intro paragraph as never revealed on mobile; mobile-page-02 shows it rendered but collided with the logo - either way the customer cannot read it cleanly.

ref-0002.customer: Founder, CEO or CFO of an established company (20-250+ employees, any industry) that needs cash for growth without raising equity or debt, and is wary about privacy, customer contracts and reputation. Five questions: (1) How much would my company get? (2) Will my customers' and staff's private info leak - is this safe and legal? (3) Who ends up with my data - could it reach competitors? (4) How much work is this for my team? (5) Who is Replay, and has anyone like me actually done this?

five_questions_test.question: How much would my company actually get?
five_questions_test.where: desktop-page-04 only: $10K-$100K (20-50 employees), $100K-$1M (50-250); on mobile-page-04 the bars show no amounts, and report.json lists '$10K - $100K', '$100K - $1M', '$1,000,000+' among 15 elements still invisible after scrolling and under reduced motion

five_questions_test.question: Will private information about my customers and staff leak?
five_questions_test.where: mobile-page-06 / desktop-page-06: 'Your data leaves cleaner than a medical record' - HIPAA's 18 categories plus 60+, names, emails, API keys; redacted-email demo

five_questions_test.question: Who ends up with my data?
five_questions_test.where: mobile-page-07 / desktop-page-07: 'only sold to frontier AI and data labs' and 'never sold to foreign adversaries or resold through brokers'

five_questions_test.question: How much work is this for my team?
five_questions_test.where: desktop-page-05 'Four steps. 120 minutes of your time.'; on mobile the heading is not visible in any capture - mobile-page-05 shows only step 1 'Get a valuation' with Terms/Protect/Payout collapsed

five_questions_test.question: Who is Replay and has a business like mine done this?
five_questions_test.where: not answered: only 'Millions - Paid to businesses like yours' (mobile-page-02, measured 3.15:1 contrast), no named customers, testimonials, team or funding; footer shows 'Sunsets HQ Corp.' at 10 px

reasons.customer:
The copy speaks the owner's language and answers payout size, privacy, buyer and effort plainly - better than most - but every answer comes after 'Value my data' and trust/proof is missing.
The money ranges are hidden on mobile and under reduced motion, proof captions are grey-on-light at 3.15:1, and a cookie bar covers the bottom ~14% of every mobile screen.

claims.claim: Mostly small type gives a neat impression
claims.evidence: Wrong on 'mostly': the headlines are large serifs (mobile sizes 42/39/36/28 px; desktop 72/64 px) and those are what stay readable. Where the type is small, it hurts the customer: 14 font sizes on desktop and 16 on mobile; tiny-text FAILs at 8 px ('process', 'identified', 'Historical operating data'), 7 px ('classification: proprietary data / licensing', industry labels 'Tech', 'Legal', 'Finance' at 7.16 px), 6.8 px, and 2.8/2.3 px on mobile; running text at 14-14.5 px ('Headcount is a proxy...', 'You're paid up front...'). The small text is also low-contrast: #aaaaaa on #fcfcfc = 2.26:1, #8d8d8d = 3.24:1, #898989 = 3.41:1, the proof caption 'Paid to businesses like yours' #919191 on #fff = 3.15:1, body #727272 on #eaebf1 = 4.04:1. On mobile-page-02 the 'PROCESS: IDENTIFIED -> STRUCTURED...' strip is grey micro-type that cannot be read at arm's length. Neat to a designer; illegible to a 50-year-old CFO on a phone.

take: Self-locating payout table: headcount bands mapped to dollar ranges ('20-50 employees: $10K-$100K') under a heading in the customer's words ('What companies your size get paid') - desktop-page-04. Render the numbers as static text, not an animated reveal.
State the effort in minutes: 'Four steps. 120 minutes of your time.' (desktop-page-05) answers the 'how much work' objection in one line.

Answer the fear with a familiar benchmark plus an explicit negative list: 'cleaner than a medical record' (HIPAA's 18 categories + 60 more) and 'never sold to foreign adversaries or resold through brokers' - mobile-page-06/07.
avoid: Micro-type for meaning: 8, 7, 6.8 and 2.8 px text on mobile, 14 px running copy, and grey proof captions at 2.26:1-3.41:1 contrast.

Hiding the most important number behind animation: 15 text elements including '$10K - $100K', '$100K - $1M', '$1,000,000+' and 'Receive an offer' stay invisible after scrolling and under reduced motion; mobile-page-04 shows bars with no amounts.
Persistent cookie bar covering ~120 of 844 px (about 14%) on every mobile capture (mobile-fold through mobile-page-10), plus 12 tap targets under 24 px (e.g. 63x16 'Overview', 95x16 'How it works').
missed_by_note: The type problem is not 'neat vs. busy' but legibility and contrast - the claim misses measured 2.26:1-3.41:1 grey text and sub-8 px labels.
The single most persuasive answer (dollar ranges by company size) is invisible on mobile and with reduced motion.
No proof of who Replay is or who has been paid: 'Millions' is unquantified, no names, logos, quotes or team.
Does not address 'am I even allowed to sell this?' (customer contracts, NDAs, employee consent).
Cookie bar obscures content on every mobile screen.

ref-0003.customer: Owner or general manager of an independent US liquor store (1-5 locations) running a 1990s-era Windows POS or a restaurant POS, losing hours to manual invoices and stock counts. Five questions: (1) What does it cost, including card fees? (2) How painful is switching - will I lose my catalog, will the store go down? (3) Does it really handle liquor stuff (thousands of SKUs, distributors, invoices, cases vs bottles, ID checks)? (4) Does it work with my delivery apps, ecommerce and hardware? (5) Are stores like mine using it and happy?

five_questions_test.question: What does it cost, including card fees?
five_questions_test.where: not on the page: 'lowest fees guaranteed' with no number (mobile-page-04, desktop-page-05); 'Pricing' is a nav link on desktop-fold and only a footer link on mobile-page-08

five_questions_test.question: How painful is switching from my old system?
five_questions_test.where: not answered; 'The old way' section (mobile-page-05, desktop-page-07) names the pain but says nothing about data migration, training, or downtime

five_questions_test.question: Does it actually handle liquor-store work?
five_questions_test.where: desktop-fold / mobile-fold product screenshot with real liquor SKUs, stock status, distributor filter and order forecast; 'Automatically read invoices', 'Optimize stock and margins' (mobile-page-03); invoice-matching screen (mobile-page-06). ID/age verification never mentioned

five_questions_test.question: Does it work with my delivery apps, website and hardware?
five_questions_test.where: mobile-page-03/04, desktop-page-04/05: 'synced to delivery apps, ecommerce... No double entry, no out-of-stock orders... API'; Uber Eats tiles; terminal and customer display shown (mobile-page-04, desktop-page-06); 'Keep selling - even offline' (mobile-page-05)

five_questions_test.question: Are stores like mine using it?
five_questions_test.where: mobile-page-02 / desktop-page-02-03: retailer logos (Big Bear, Applejack, Green's, JAX, Buster's) and named owners/GMs (Cheers, Bacchus, Simmons Liquor) - but the testimony is video-only, no written quote; '20% less time spent on inventory management' (desktop-page-04)

reasons.customer:
Instantly clear who it is for, with liquor-specific screens, recognisable store owners and an 'old way' scene a store owner will recognise; integration and offline worries are answered.
But price, card-fee numbers and switching effort - the two things that decide a POS replacement - are missing, and the only path is 'Book a demo' (3.60:1 contrast).

take: Old way / new way with the customer's own artefacts: a 90s Windows item form, a paper distributor invoice and a sticky note saying 'Adjust inventory' (mobile-page-05, desktop-page-06/07) - the owner sees their own back office.

Product screenshots filled with real catalogue data (New Riff Sour Mash, Château Pape Clément, 'Out of Stock', distributor filter) so the owner recognises their own inventory in the fold - mobile-fold.
Named peers on camera with store names and job titles, plus regional retailer logos, under a heading in the customer's words ('Liquor store owners, in their own words') - mobile-page-02.
avoid: Unquantified money claims and a demo-only path: 'lowest fees guaranteed' with no rate, no price on the page, and 'Book a demo' as the main CTA at white on #f54900 = 3.60:1.
Testimonials locked in video: no pull-quote text, so an owner scanning at the counter gets names but no words; 2 images without alt.

Interaction and motion hiding content: tab buttons measured 109x2 px ('Ordering', 'Receiving', 'Analytics') and 'Find out more' 111x20 px; 12 text elements incl. 'POS & Payments', 'Hardware for every store', 'The new way' stay hidden under reduced motion; 'Designed with support from top retailers' #666 on #000 = 3.66:1; footer 2.48:1.
missed_by_note: No designer note was supplied for this reference, so nothing to verify.
Pricing and payment-fee numbers are absent despite 'lowest fees guaranteed'.
Switching/migration (catalogue import, training, downtime) - the core fear of someone replacing an old POS - is never addressed.
Age/ID verification, a liquor-specific compliance need, is not mentioned.
Customer stories are video-only; add one written quote per card.
